title: nvml-syscall-timeout-notes
content:
Summary:
Intermittent NVML timeouts observed on c6g-inference nodes during stress runs. Symptoms: nvidia-smi (and any process calling libnvidia-ml) hangs for >30s and then returns NVML_ERROR_TIMEOUT. No deterministic reproducer yet; happens under sustained allocation + concurrent context switching. This file is a scratchpad of commands tried, output snippets, and hypotheses to triage further.

Repro steps I used locally (non-root test container):
$ python tests/gpu_mem_ramp.py --alloc-step 200M --hold 10 --iterations 40
# simple loop: allocate X, touch memory, sleep, free

Observed behavior:
- At ~18GB allocated on a T4 (driver 525.105, kernel 6.4), first hang appears. nvidia-smi blocks for 32s, then exits with: "NVMLError: NVML_ERROR_TIMEOUT".
- strace on nvidia-smi: stuck in ioctl call repeatedly; timestamps show ~30s stall.
- dmesg around the event: 
  [ 12345.678901] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: GPU fault: ISR timeout
  [ 12345.679102] nvidia: nvml: syscall timeout in nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo
  [ 12345.679203] pci 0000:01:00.0: link down, resetting link
  [ 12345.789345] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: GPU reported page fault on address 0x7f8abcde
- system logs show repeated "Kernel oops?" like messages previously on other runs.

Key command traces (snippets):
$ strace -f -t -o /tmp/strace-nvml.log nvidia-smi
[13:02:15] ioctl(3, NVML_IOCTL_DEVICE_GET_MEMORY_INFO, ...) = -1 EIO (I/O error)  # blocks here for ~32s
# after ~32s
[13:02:47] ioctl(3, NVML_IOCTL_DEVICE_GET_MEMORY_INFO, ...) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
# nvidia-smi prints: "NVMLError: NVML_ERROR_TIMEOUT"

$ gdb -p <pid of hung process> backtrace
# thread 1 (gdb excerpt)
#0  0x00007f8... in ioctl () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6
#1  0x00007f8... in nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
#2  main_loop () at nvidia-smi.cpp:421
#3  __libc_start_main

What I tried so far (quick list):
- Reproduced minimal alloc script to isolate from Python ML stack. Same hang reproduced.
- kernel: 6.1 vs 6.4 comparison (two identical baremetal images). Problem more frequent on 6.4; not 100% exclusive.
- Driver versions: 515.x vs 525.x vs 535.x. 525 shows most occurrences in our fleet.
- Reinstalled drivers (apt purge nvidia-* && apt install nvidia-driver-525) and rebooted — short-term relief on one node, recurrence after a few stress rounds.
- Set nvidia-persistenced enabled on boot; reduced frequency but did not eliminate.
- LD_PRELOAD experiments: preloading libnvidia-ml.so changed where hang manifested (moved earlier to allocation stage), but did not remove timeout.
- Disabled power-management features on GPU (NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1) — experimental; no clear effect.
- Tried running inside --gpus=all Docker container vs host; same failures (so likely kernel/driver interaction, not container cgroups).

Additional logs captured (paste excerpts):
----- /var/log/syslog -----
Mar  3 13:02:14 node-42 kernel: [12345.678901] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: firmware timeout, resetting
Mar  3 13:02:15 node-42 kernel: [12345.679102] nvml: syscall timeout in nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo: id=0
Mar  3 13:02:47 node-42 kernel: [12345.789345] pci 0000:01:00.0: device not responding, recovered
----- end -----

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NVML <-> kernel driver ABI drift: occasional ioctl codepath returns EIO when driver is in a transient state (driver update/partial init). But fleet shows same driver across nodes, so why intermittent?
2) PCIe link flaps under high memory pressure causing driver to reset GPU mid-IOCTL, leading to NVML timeouts. dmesg shows "link down" messages sometimes correlated.
3) Firmware (VBIOS) or GPU microcontroller entering a stuck state when allocations touch specific pages (e.g., large contiguous pages on Turing SM). Page faults shown in dmesg hint at this.
4) Kernel scheduling / preemption: heavy context switching with many CUDA contexts may starve the driver watchdog, causing timeout on user-space wait for kernel event.
5) Subtle bug in our allocation pattern (touching pinned pages) that triggers driver bug on specific hardware.

Things that improved but did not fully fix:
- nvidia-persistenced+keepalive script to keep driver warmed up reduced frequency by ~40% (empirical).
- downgrading to 515.x reduced occurrences in a small sample (N=3) but increased regressions for other workloads.

Next experiments to run (todo):
- Capture full nvmetrace (nv-host engine traces) and gpu firmware logs around event. Contact infra for kernel-level tracing (ftrace on nvidia_{module}_handler).
- Run pci-rescan loop to see if forcing link retrain triggers the bug reproducibly.
- Bisect driver: spin up test nodes with 515/520/525/535 and run long ramp to get frequency metrics (we have 6 nodes available).
- Add probe: when nvml ioctl hangs, trigger kdump or save GPU error state via /sys/kernel/debug/dri/0/* if available.
- Reproduce with MIG slices disabled (if applicable) to rule out slice-level isolation bug.

Quick checklist for next on-call runbook (if this happens during customer job):
- Step 0: Do not kill the process immediately; capture strace and gdb backtrace (attach, bt all).
- Step 1: Check dmesg and /var/log/syslog for "link down" or "firmware timeout" lines.
- Step 2: Try nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY (might succeed after 30s); copy output and /proc/driver/nvidia/version.
- Step 3: If IOCTL timeouts repeat and node unstable, cordon node and schedule reboot; collect nvflash/firmware info to attach to ticket.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is there a known NVML timeout constant mapped to a driver state we can check? (ask NVIDIA rep).
- Does enabling 'NVreg_RegistryDwords' debug flags expose more info? (RFC to infra).
- Consider adding guard in runtime: if NVML timeout occurs, fallback to cached memory stats instead of blocking upstream request.

Relevant artifacts and quick refs:
- host reproduce script: tests/gpu_mem_ramp.py (attached to INF-2048 ticket)
- quick grep for "NVML_ERROR_TIMEOUT" in fleet logs: /srv/logs/gpu/*.gz (ran on 2026-03-05)

Notes timestamped:
2026-02-10 11:14 - initial repro and first capture
2026-02-15 09:06 - tried nvidia-persistenced mitigation
2026-03-03 13:05 - saw link down in dmesg; opened INF-2048
2026-03-08 16:21 - hardware team scheduled node for firmware extract

End of scratchpad.

-- marisol
